subject: general
question: What did the Champaran movement protest against?

options.text: Financial atrocities by the British government
Extra taxation by the land lords

solution:
The correct answer is__** Forced cultivation of indigo**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Champaran movement** protested against the **forced cultivation of indigo** 
 
• It began in 1917 in the Champaran district of Bihar, where farmers were being compelled by British planters to grow indigo on a portion of their land under the **Tinkathia system**.
 
• This system was highly exploitative, as the indigo crop was sold at very low prices, leaving the farmers in poverty.
 
• The movement, led by **Mahatma Gandhi**, aimed to end this oppressive practice and marked his first major involvement in India's freedom struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Financial atrocities by the British government**:

 
 
• This refers to the various exploitative financial policies imposed by the British, such as heavy land revenue systems and excessive taxes.
 
• These policies placed severe economic pressure on Indian farmers and common people, leading to widespread poverty and discontent.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act, 1919**:
 
 
• This draconian law allowed the British government to arrest and imprison Indians without trial, suppressing civil liberties.
 
• It led to widespread protests across India, culminating in events like the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**
 
 
 
• **Extra taxation by landlords**:
 
 
• This refers to the exploitative practices by zamindars (landlords) who imposed heavy taxes and rents on farmers.
 
• While this was a common issue in many parts of India, the Champaran movement specifically addressed the forced cultivation of indigo rather than extra taxation.
